feedback: Iteration 1 (narrow row at plus or minus 0.02 m, y=0.04, 12 mm) scored 57.11, up from 51.09 at iteration 0, but the stall progress stayed at 0.155 on the oval and s-bend, and every run still went off track at max error about 0.063. Slalom oscillation fell only from 0.153 to 0.150. So narrowing the row and moving it forward did not change oscillation much; the controller change was also in that race, so the two effects are confounded. The off-track limit of 0.06 m is still the binding failure. Based on this evidence, I recommend holding the geometry for iteration 2 so the new controller is judged on it. For the next geometry, the key open question is coverage. With a 12 mm footprint on the narrow row, the last sensor sees tape only until an offset of about 0.038 m, so the robot gets little warning before the 0.06 m limit. If the next race shows line loss at progress above 0.1 on a bend, try a wider row. If it shows line loss near progress 0, the coverage edge is not the cause, and the geometry should not change.
requested_changes: Hold sensor_positions, sensor_size and wheel geometry for iteration 2, so the controller change is measured on a known platform. Next iteration, if line loss still appears after progress 0.1, try a wider row at x = plus or minus 0.03 m with sensor_size 0.016 (reach about 0.05 m), which gives more warning before the 0.06 m limit.

If the next race shows slalom steering oscillation still at or above 0.15 with the geometry held, try a forward offset of y = 0.02 with the same row. Iteration 1 moved the row from y=0.06 to y=0.04 and oscillation barely changed, so this is a second, smaller step; do not expect it to fix the oscillation alone.
Ask the Integrator to report the progress at the first line-loss event on each track, and the max error at that moment. This separates coverage-edge loss from controller overshoot.
